cards.front: The first antenatal (booking) visit should ideally be before [___] weeks; first-trimester crown-rump length provides accurate pregnancy dating.
cards.context:
Early booking matters for two reasons: dating accuracy is highest before 14 weeks (CRL), and time-sensitive interventions start in T1 — folate continuation, smoking cessation, asymptomatic bacteriuria treatment.

Late booking (>14 weeks) misses these windows + forces less accurate later-pregnancy dating.

Rushing → missed teratogen or unrecognised mental health condition.

cards.front: The drug used to treat and prevent seizures in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia is [___].
cards.context:
Eclampsia = pre-eclampsia plus a tonic-clonic seizure.

The drug that both treats the seizure and prevents recurrence (and is used as prophylaxis in severe pre-eclampsia) is magnesium sulfate — NOT a standard anticonvulsant.

cards.front: Preconception planning should begin 3-6 months before conception; the five pillars include folate, lifestyle, medication review, chronic disease control, and reproductive [___] screening.
cards.context:
The 3-6 month window matters because highest-risk fetal development precedes a recognised pregnancy. The neural tube closes by day 28 and organogenesis is done by 12 weeks, so optimisation must precede conception.

Five pillars: folate; lifestyle (smoking, alcohol, weight); medication review (switch teratogens: warfarin, ACEi/ARB, methotrexate, isotretinoin); carrier screening (identify carrier couples early).

Plus chronic disease control: diabetes, epilepsy, SLE and thyroid stable BEFORE conception, when first-trimester glycaemia and disease activity set anomaly and miscarriage risk.

cards.front: Anti-D should be given within [___] hours of a sensitising event in Rh-negative women; still give if delayed because partial protection persists.
cards.context:
The 72-hour window is when passive anti-D antibody can clear circulating fetal D-positive red cells before maternal B cells encounter the D antigen and start producing endogenous IgM, then IgG, alloantibodies.

Beyond 72 hours sensitisation may have begun, but a late dose still gives some protection, so give it up to 10 days after the event.

cards.front: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a screening test analysing cell-free fetal DNA from [___] weeks; positive results require invasive CVS/amniocentesis confirmation.
cards.context:
NIPT analyses cell-free fetal DNA fragments shed by placental trophoblast into maternal blood. The 10-week floor is when fetal fraction is high enough to call reliably; earlier risks an uninterpretable 'no result'.

It is a SCREENING test, not diagnostic — the DNA is placental, not directly fetal, so a positive can be confined placental mosaicism, a vanishing twin, or maternal mosaicism.

That is why a positive must be confirmed by an invasive karyotype (CVS or amniocentesis) before any irreversible decision.

cards.front: Trial of labour after caesarean: baseline uterine rupture risk is approximately [___]% in experienced centres; risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation. Overall TOLAC success rate is around 70%.
cards.context:
VBAC carries a small but real risk of uterine rupture along the previous scar — ~1:200 (0.5%) in experienced centres for a single previous transverse lower segment CS.

Risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation (over-stimulation stresses scar), rises with prior classical (vertical) incision (~5-10% — generally contraindicates VBAC), multiple previous CS.

VBAC success rate ~70%, lower without prior vaginal birth + recurrent CS indication.

cards.front: Standard newborn vitamin K prophylaxis is [___] IM at birth — single dose, near-100% effective for VKDB.
cards.context:
Newborns are vitamin K deficient because: placenta poorly transfers vitamin K, gut is sterile (no bacterial production), liver synthesis of factors II/VII/IX/X requires vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation.

IM 1 mg at birth is single-dose, near-100% effective for both classical and late VKDB. The 1992 leukaemia link has been refuted by multiple subsequent large studies.

cards.front: NT >=3.5 mm — a separate, fixed threshold above the >95th-centile aneuploidy-screening cutoff — is independently associated with structural anomalies including [___] defects.
cards.context:
Increased NT (>95th centile for CRL, roughly 2.1-2.8 mm across the 11-14 week window) is a non-specific marker of fetal stress — fluid accumulation behind the fetal neck from any cause altering lymphatic drainage.

This is the aneuploidy-screening trigger. NT ≥3.5 mm is a separate, higher, fixed cutoff independently associated with cardiac and other structural anomalies, regardless of the aneuploidy screening result.

Picks up aneuploidies (T21, T18, T13, monosomy X), structural anomalies (cardiac, diaphragmatic hernia), and genetic syndromes with normal karyotype.

cards.front: After in-utero opioid exposure, formal abstinence scoring begins within [___] of birth.
cards.context:
Either a Finnegan score or eat-sleep-console assessment is started on that clock, including before signs appear.

Non-opioid exposure is different: routine formal scoring waits unless the baby actually shows signs.

cards.front: The [___] trial (2019) showed ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) does not reduce adverse perinatal outcomes in intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP); the most important intervention is delivery timing based on bile acid level.
cards.context:
UDCA was the standard ICP treatment for decades on observational evidence.

UDCA remains widely used for symptomatic relief but focus shifted to delivery timing as the single most outcome-influencing intervention.

Weekly bile acid monitoring catches escalating disease.

cards.front: Bacterial vaginosis is a polymicrobial dysbiosis (Gardnerella, Mobiluncus, Atopobium replacing the Lactobacillus-dominated normal flora). It recurs in [___]% of women within 3 months — the 2025 StepUp RCT found concurrent male-partner treatment reduces recurrence in heterosexual couples.
cards.context:
BV is anaerobic dysbiosis: Gardnerella, Mobiluncus and Atopobium overgrow as Lactobacillus-dominated flora is lost.

Recurrence is common. The 2025 StepUp RCT found concurrent male-partner metronidazole plus topical clindamycin reduced 12-week recurrence in heterosexual couples.

cards.front: Chorioamnionitis usually results from [___] infection, not from spread through the maternal bloodstream.
cards.context:
Ascending means organisms move up from the vagina, not through the mother's bloodstream. The membranes can then become inflamed.

That process can also inflame the cord: umbilical vasculitis and funisitis. Those cord findings point to ascent.

A vaginal swab shows colonisation only. It does not separate ascent from contact with lesions or blood during birth.

cards.front: Elevated middle cerebral artery (MCA) peak systolic velocity (>1.5 multiples of the median) suggests fetal [___]; treatment may require intrauterine transfusion.
cards.context:
Fetal anaemia drops blood viscosity, which paradoxically RAISES peak systolic velocity in the MCA — the brain compensates for reduced O₂ carriage by increasing flow.

When PSV crosses threshold, refer urgently to MFM for IUT via cordocentesis.

cards.front: MRI without contrast is considered safe in pregnancy; the contrast agent limited because of an uncertain fetal effect is [___].
cards.context:
MRI without contrast does not use ionising radiation and is considered safe in pregnancy. The uncertainty sits with the contrast, not the magnet.

Iodinated CT contrast is a different agent and is described as safe when the scan is indicated.

cards.front: APGAR components (each 0-2, total 0-10): Appearance (colour), Pulse, Grimace (reflex), Activity (tone), [___]. Assessed at 1 minutes after birth and again at 5 minutes.
cards.context:
APGAR is a 5-component bedside assessment at 1 and 5 min (and q5min if low).

It documents the infant's condition and response to resuscitation — it does NOT trigger resuscitation, which is guided by breathing, heart rate and tone assessed within seconds of birth (AAP/ACOG).

The ranges (7-10 vigorous, 4-6 moderately depressed, 0-3 severely depressed) describe status, not a resuscitation recipe.

cards.front: Severe-range hypertension in pregnancy: SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110 mmHg; treat urgently to reduce maternal [___] risk.
cards.context:
Severe-range HTN in pregnancy (SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110) is a hypertensive emergency — cerebral autoregulation breaks down, vasculature can't constrict adequately.

Treat acutely: IV hydralazine 5-10 mg, IV labetalol 20 mg (avoid in asthma), or oral nifedipine IR 10 mg — repeat q15-30 min until BP <160/110.

Don't aim for normotension: a precipitous drop collapses pressure-dependent uteroplacental perfusion, causing fetal distress. Target SBP 140-150, DBP 90-100 first hours, then oral (methyldopa, labetalol, nifedipine SR).

cards.front: Preterm birth is birth between [___]+0 and 36+6 weeks; affects ~8-9% of Australian pregnancies and is the leading cause of mortality in children <5.
cards.context:
Gestation is written weeks+days, so 20+0 = 20 weeks 0 days and 36+6 = the last day before 37 weeks (term); the 20-week floor is the same threshold that separates preterm birth from miscarriage.

Sub-categorised by severity: late preterm (34-36+6, ~70% of cases, generally good outcomes), moderate (32-33+6), very preterm (28-31+6, significant NICU need), and extremely preterm (<28 weeks).

Even late preterm infants have higher rates of learning difficulties, ADHD, and reduced educational attainment than term peers — which is why prevention matters even near term.

cards.front: Active management of the third stage of labour gives oxytocin [___] IU IM at or soon after birth of the anterior shoulder.
cards.context:
Active management of the third stage is oxytocin 10 IU IM at or soon after birth of the anterior shoulder, then controlled cord traction once the placenta has separated.

Compared with physiological management it reduces blood loss, severe PPH and transfusion.

Give it shortly after birth: Australian guidance reports no significant PPH difference between giving it before or after the placenta, so a late dose is no reason to omit it.

cards.front: Severe unconjugated neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia can leave permanent neurological injury called [___].
cards.context: Kernicterus refers to the permanent neurological sequelae of bilirubin toxicity. Acute bilirubin encephalopathy describes the acute clinical syndrome.

cards.front: Recurrent miscarriage is now defined as [___] or more pregnancy losses <20 weeks (down from the previous 3+ threshold).
cards.context:
Recurrent miscarriage is defined as two or more confirmed intrauterine pregnancy losses before 20 weeks. Important actionable causes include antiphospholipid syndrome and uterine anomalies.

Test for anticardiolipin, lupus anticoagulant and anti-β2GP1; positivity must persist at least 12 weeks apart to confirm APS.

Analyse pregnancy tissue when available. Consider parental karyotyping case by case, including when tissue analysis is unavailable.

cards.front: The classic triad of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is amenorrhoea, vaginal bleeding, and unilateral [___].
cards.context:
The classic triad occurs in only about half of ectopic pregnancies; presentations may include GI symptoms, shoulder-tip pain or syncope.

Risk rises after previous ectopic, tubal damage or surgery, IVF, or pregnancy with an IUD in situ. Assess with TVUS and serial βhCG; an empty uterus above the local threshold is concerning but not diagnostic.

Rupture with instability needs urgent surgery. Stable, eligible patients with low βhCG and no fetal cardiac activity may be considered for methotrexate.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation: start positive pressure ventilation (PPV) if HR <100 or no spontaneous breathing; ventilation is the priority because most neonatal arrests are [___] in origin.
cards.context:
Neonatal resus algorithm: first 30 sec — dry, stimulate, keep warm, position airway. 30-sec reassessment: if breathing inadequately OR HR <100.

After 30 sec PPV: HR rising + breathing improving → continue support and wean; HR remains <100 → optimise ventilation (MR SOPA); HR <60 despite effective ventilation → add chest compressions 3:1 with breaths.

cards.front: Elevated middle cerebral artery (MCA) peak systolic velocity (>[___] multiples of the median) suggests fetal anaemia; treatment may require intrauterine transfusion.
cards.context:
Fetal anaemia drops blood viscosity, which paradoxically RAISES peak systolic velocity in the MCA — the brain compensates for reduced O₂ carriage by increasing flow.

When PSV crosses threshold, refer urgently to MFM for IUT via cordocentesis.

cards.front: Average expected weight gain in a normal-BMI singleton pregnancy is approximately 12.5 kg, with most gained after [___] weeks.
cards.context:
The 12.5 kg figure is an average for a normal-BMI singleton pregnancy; IOM ranges scale by pre-pregnancy BMI: underweight (BMI <18.5) 12.5-18 kg, normal (18.5-24.9) 11.5-16 kg, overweight (25-29.9) 7-11.5 kg.

Breakdown: only ~3.5 kg is fetus; rest is amniotic fluid (~1.5 kg), uterus (~1 kg), breasts (~1 kg), plasma volume + maternal fat stores (~5 kg).

cards.front: Initial drug treatment of PPH uses [___] as a uterotonic plus early tranexamic acid 1 g IV as an antifibrinolytic adjunct; avoid ergometrine in HTN and carboprost in asthma.
cards.context:
Treat PPH concurrently: start uterine massage and an appropriate uterotonic such as oxytocin, and give tranexamic acid 1 g IV as soon as possible and within 3 hours of birth.

Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic adjunct, not a uterotonic; a second 1 g dose may be given after 30 minutes if bleeding persists under the protocol.

Escalate uterotonics per protocol. Avoid ergometrine in hypertension or pre-eclampsia and carboprost in asthma.

cards.front: The Safer Baby Bundle's five care elements include [___] cessation, growth surveillance, awareness of decreased fetal movements, side-sleeping position from 28 weeks, and individualised timing of birth.
cards.context:
The bundle combines risk reduction, early recognition of fetal compromise and shared decisions.

Birth timing reflects each woman's risks and preferences; it is not a fixed early-delivery rule.

cards.front: Birth before [___] completed weeks of gestation is defined as preterm.
cards.context:
The definition is by gestation, not weight: birth before 37 completed weeks.

It's the leading cause of death and long-term disability in under-5s, which is why prevention and the steroid/magnesium 'bundle' matter so much.

cards.front: The newborn bloodspot screens for treatable conditions including PKU, congenital hypothyroidism and [___].
cards.context:
The newborn bloodspot ('heel-prick' / Guthrie) screens around day 2–3 for treatable conditions where early detection prevents serious harm.

Examples: PKU, congenital hypothyroidism, cystic fibrosis, and several metabolic disorders.

cards.front: During CPR in pregnancy >20 weeks, perform manual [___] uterine displacement to relieve aortocaval compression.
cards.context:
From ~20 weeks, the gravid uterus compresses the IVC and aorta when the patient is supine, dropping venous return up to 70%.

So chest compressions during cardiac arrest are largely empty unless the uterus is shifted off the great vessels.

Manual left uterine displacement (pull the uterus to the patient's left) is preferred — it doesn't compromise compressions or airway; the older 15-30° tilt works but compromises both.
